titlePattern.gap: No top-10 title compares several heads by name for real estate; most are single-owner picks or forum threads. Ours leads with the exact keyword and promises 6 geared heads compared (no year: only 1 of 10 titles has one).

commonPoints: Use a geared head, not a ball head, for interiors and architecture: ball heads shift several axes at once and can sag (APALMANAC, Jak Spedding, Show&Tour, Rick McEvoy).
The Manfrotto 410 Junior is the classic entry geared head, but it uses Manfrotto's own 410PL plate (APALMANAC, Jak Spedding, DPReview thread).
The Arca-Swiss d4 is the premium choice, expensive but light for its load (APALMANAC, Jak Spedding, Show&Tour).
Benro and K&F Concept geared heads are the value Arca-type options (Show&Tour, Digital Camera World, DPReview thread).
Buy the best head you can afford; cheap heads are a false economy (APALMANAC, Jak Spedding).

ourGain.point: Load headroom against a real interior kit (Rick McEvoy's Canon 6D + 17-40mm, 1.25 kg): the 4 kg XPRO gives 3.2x, the 410's 5 kg 4x, the Benro and K&F 6 kg 4.8x, the 405's 7.5 kg 6x, the d4's 30 kg 24x. Every head clears the /how-we-score/ 3x mark for that kit; only the XPRO gets tight once a heavier body and L-bracket go on.
ourGain.source: maker specs (Manfrotto, Benro, K&F, Arca-Swiss USA) + Rick McEvoy's stated kit weight

ourGain.point: Carry weight across a day of houses: the Manfrotto 405 (1.6 kg) weighs more than twice the XPRO geared (0.75 kg) and almost twice the Benro GD3WH (0.87 kg).

Pick the plate system first: if your bodies already wear Arca-type plates or an L-bracket, the Benro, K&F or d4 drop in; the Manfrotto 410/405 (410PL) and XPRO (200PL) need their own plates or an Arca clamp adapter.
ourGain.source: maker specs + DPReview owners (Abbott Schindler, MikeInOr)

ourGain.point: The clamp and stock plate fail before the gears: Nathan Cool broke a Benro two-stage clamp knob and found the K&F stock plate slips; fix = do not over-torque the Benro knob, swap the K&F plate for a 70 mm Arca plate.

painPoints.pain: A budget ball head drops a little after you tighten it, so the framing shifts
painPoints.details: Owners report a ball head settling after tightening; for interiors that undoes a leveled frame, which is why the top pages push geared heads.

quotes.text: The ball head drops about a centimeter after you tighten it but after that it doesn't move at all.

painPoints.pain: A quick release plate from one tripod does not fit another brand's head
painPoints.details: Manfrotto geared heads use the 410PL plate; owners add an Arca clamp on top or buy an adapter.

quotes.text: Its drawback is that it uses an odd Manfrotto QR plate.

painPoints.pain: Leveling a tripod by adjusting the legs on uneven ground takes forever
painPoints.details: A geared head's roll and pitch knobs level the camera without touching the legs.

quotes.text: Leveling the load by adjusting legs is an exercise in pain and frustration

painPoints.pain: The Arca-type plate that ships with a budget geared head lets the camera twist
painPoints.details: Nathan Cool found the K&F stock plate moves on any head; he recommends a 70 mm plate with good grip material.

quotes.text: The KNF plate that comes with the KNF head is terrible.

painPoints.pain: The clamp knob on a geared head breaks or sticks when over-tightened
painPoints.details: Nathan Cool broke the two-stage clamp knob on one Benro head and had another stick.

quotes.text: On one Benro head, I actually did break that.
